raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

- The gateway's `http_request` span always starts a new trace, even when the caller sent a `traceparent`, so the caller's trace and SGLang's are disconnected.
- A request the gateway rejects (no worker, rate limit, bad request) never reaches an engine, so the gateway's span is the only record of it, and that span carries no request ID a caller would know.
- 4xx/5xx responses aren't marked on the span, so samplers and alerts that key on errors can't see gateway failures.

The existing `--request-id-headers` doesn't cover the second point: it picks the first matching header as a single `request_id` (generating one if none is present) for correlation inside the gateway. It doesn't record the raw values of several IDs, and the engine never sees what it picked.

## Modifications

1. **Continue incoming W3C traces and record request IDs.**
   - `RequestSpan` sets the span's parent from an incoming `traceparent` (`extract_trace_context_http`).
   - Request headers named in `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` are recorded on the span as `http.request.header.<name>`, cut to 1024 bytes. This is the same variable, attribute name and limit as the engine (#<request-headers PR>), so one setting covers both. Header values are visible ASCII, so bytes and characters agree.
   - Headers named in `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` or the existing `SGLANG_LOG_REQUEST_HEADERS` are forwarded to workers, so the engine can record or log them too.
   - `ResponseLogger` records an `error` attribute on 4xx/5xx (the router's error code, or the HTTP reason phrase) and sets `otel.status_code=ERROR` on 5xx only, following the OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions for server spans.
2. **Don't forward hop-by-hop and framing headers named in those lists.** If a list names a hop-by-hop header (`host`, `connection`, `transfer-encoding`, `proxy-authorization`, ...) or `content-length` (say, to log it on the engine), copying the client's value onto the request the gateway builds for the worker would misroute or misframe it. Those are skipped with a warning, reusing the hop-by-hop list the gateway already applies to worker responses (`should_forward_header_no_alloc`). Other listed headers are recorded and forwarded as configured.
3. **Docs** in `production_request_trace.mdx`.

### Behavior changes

- `http_request` spans join the caller's trace when a valid `traceparent` is present; before, they always started a new one.
- 4xx/5xx responses record `error`; 5xx responses mark the span as an error.
- With neither header variable set in the gateway's environment, no headers are recorded and forwarding is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. Per request: one `traceparent` extraction, plus one header lookup per configured header. The configured lists are parsed once (`OnceLock`).

## Tests

- `middleware::tests::test_request_span_continues_incoming_w3c_trace`
- `middleware::tests::test_request_span_records_request_ids`
- `middleware::tests::test_request_span_cuts_recorded_headers_to_1024_bytes`
- `header_utils::tests::test_configured_hop_by_hop_and_framing_headers_are_not_forwarded`
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, spans exported to Jaeger), with the gateway in front of a regular TP=2 server and, separately, in PD mode in front of prefill and decode servers. In both setups:
  - A request with a caller `traceparent` produced one trace: caller span → gateway `http_request` → engine root span(s).
  - The gateway and engine spans recorded the configured request IDs.
  - With `host` and `content-length` named in the lists, the gateway logged its warning and each engine saw the gateway's own `host`.
  - A 400 recorded `error` without ERROR status.
- In the regular setup, with the engine stopped, the gateway's 500 recorded `error=call_upstream_request_error` with ERROR status.
- `cargo test --lib --tests`: 855 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo +nightly fmt -- --check` are clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable: no model-output change.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -38,6 +38,8 @@ This section explains how to configure the request tracing and export the trace
 
     Replace `0.0.0.0:4317` with the actual endpoint of the OpenTelemetry collector. If you launched the openTelemetry collector with tracing_compose.yaml, the default receiving port is 4317.
 
+    The model gateway continues an incoming W3C `traceparent`, so its `http_request` span joins the caller's trace. It records the request headers named in `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` on that span as `http.request.header.<name>`, and forwards the headers named in `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` or `SGLANG_LOG_REQUEST_HEADERS` to workers so they can record them too; set these variables in the gateway's environment as well. Hop-by-hop headers (such as `host`, `connection` or `transfer-encoding`) and `content-length` are not forwarded even when a list names them, since the client's values would misframe the request to the worker.
+
     To use the HTTP/protobuf span exporter, set the following environment variable and point to an HTTP endpoint, for example, `http://0.0.0.0:4318/v1/traces`.
     ```bash Command
     export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
